# ADR 0021 — Zod is the core's one library, and the core follows one naming pattern

> **In short.** In the context of data that enters the core from outside, facing hand-written validators beside the
> domain types, we decided for Zod schemas in the domain and one file naming pattern across the hexagon and against
> keeping the core free of every package, to validate data with the same schema that gives the domain its type,
> accepting one library in the core.

## Context and problem

The core validates data that enters from outside: an app's configuration at start, asset data, later the requests the
apps receive. A core that imports no package at all validates by hand, so the first data the asset pipeline loaded was
validated by hand-written parsers beside separate types; ten files of them, whose types and checks could drift apart and
whose errors named less than a schema does. Placing those files also showed that the hexagon had no one pattern for file
names, so two sessions placed the same kind of file differently.

## Decision drivers

- One definition per data shape: the schema and the type must not drift apart.
- One naming pattern, so every session places a file the same way.
- The core still touches no IO, no framework and no other part of Pixecutive.

## Considered options

- **A — Zod in the core, one naming pattern.**
- **B — No package in the core, hand-written validators.**

## Decision

Chosen: **A**, sheet hexagon-pattern of 2026-10-04, F1.

1. **Zod is the core's one library.** The import zone allows the module `zod` in every core element; any other
   package still fails. The version is 4.6.5, measured as current on 2026-10-04. `[Lint import zones]`
2. **Files follow one pattern.**
   - The domain lives in `domain/<Aggregate>/` in PascalCase, with camelCase files that carry a type suffix
     (`.interface.ts`, `.enum.ts`, `.schema.ts`).
   - Services are `application/service/<name>.service.ts`.
   - Exceptions are `<aggregate>.exception.ts` with `<aggregate>ExceptionKey.enum.ts`.
   - Adapters are `adapter/<Area>/<port>-<technology>.adapter.ts`.

   `[Agent adversarial-review]`

### Consequences

- Good, because a schema and its type cannot disagree.
- Good, because a file's name tells its role, and every session places it the same way.
- Bad, because a library update of Zod touches the core.

### Confirmation

`scripts/probe-lint.sh` turns green on a core import of `zod` and red on a core import of any other package;
`scripts/probe-architecture.sh` does the same for the architecture guard. Every schema in the core is tested in its
spec.

## Rejected

- **B — hand-written validators.** They duplicated every shape beside its type and named their errors less exactly
  than the schemas do.
